findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the throwaway project's full contents so its build can only fail on the hatchling fetch (e.g. include a package dir matching the project name or `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] bypass-selection = true`), and assert those contents in a unit test.
evidence: "write a minimal throwaway project (`pyproject.toml` with `build-backend = \"hatchling.build\"`) to a temp dir and run `[sys.executable, \"-m\", \"build\", ...]`"
Unit tests inject the runner, so only the manual acceptance criterion would catch a probe that can never pass.
findings.finding: package_index_probe treats any non-zero `python -m build` exit as 'package index unreachable'. Yet the throwaway project is specified only as a `pyproject.toml` with `build-backend = "hatchling.build"`. Hatchling's wheel step refuses a project with no shippable files ('Unable to determine which files to ship inside the wheel'). The probe would then fail on every host, including CI-like hosts with full network, and refuse `make verify` for a cause unrelated to the capability it names.
findings.location: Approach — probe 2 `package_index_probe`
scenarios: Unsandboxed developer host with working pypi access: the build of the throwaway wheel fails on file selection, and the preflight prints 'package index' failure and exits 1.
A future hatchling release tightens metadata validation: the probe starts refusing every host.
findings.suggested_fix: Write `pyproject.toml` with `[project] name="verify-host-probe" version="0"` plus `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] bypass-selection = true` (or create `verify_host_probe/__init__.py`), and add a test asserting the written files.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests asserting that the semgrep runner receives an env with SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE/SEMGREP_LOG_FILE under the probe's temp dir, and that its argv flags match those `_opengrep_validate` uses (the test may import from src/rebar).
evidence: "It points `SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE` and `SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` into its temp dir ... so a host whose home directory is unwritable is not refused"
Testing list covers pass/exit-2/no-engine for semgrep but not the env or argv passed to the runner
findings.finding: Two load-bearing behaviors are untested, and the unit tests cannot catch drift from the backend. The probe's env redirection (SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE/SEMGREP_LOG_FILE, which keeps unwritable-home hosts from being refused) has no test. Its argv duplicates `_opengrep_validate`'s flags as hand-copied knowledge with nothing guarding against drift.
findings.location: Testing; Approach — probe 3 'the same flags `_opengrep_validate` ... passes'
scenarios: A refactor drops the env override, and hosts with an unwritable HOME are wrongly refused while the unit tests stay green.
The backend changes its validate flags, and the probe validates something different from what the tests run.

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.finding: Acceptance-criteria / definition-of-done quality issues.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify `capture_output=True, text=True` for both subprocess probes (using captured stderr as the failure detail), make the `verify-host` recipe `@`-prefixed, and add a unit test asserting the runner is called with capture_output=True.
evidence: "Exit 1 on any failure, 0 and no output otherwise."
"run `[sys.executable, "-m", "build", ...]` with `timeout=300` and the inherited environment" — no capture_output stated
"`Makefile`: new `verify-host` target running the script" — no `@` prefix stated, unlike the `@$(MAKE)` verify recipe
AC: "`make verify-host` exits 0 with no output"
findings.finding: The success contract '0 and no output otherwise' is unachievable as specified. The plan never says the child processes' stdout/stderr are captured, and `python -m build` and `semgrep --validate` print copiously. The `verify-host` recipe is also not specified as silent (`@`), so make echoes the command line.
findings.location: Approach — check_verify_host.py probes 2 and 3; Makefile `verify-host` target; AC 2
scenarios: Outside the sandbox, `make verify-host` prints the recipe line plus build/semgrep logs, so AC 2 fails.
The injected-runner unit tests pass anyway because they never check how the real runner is called.
findings.suggested_fix: In probes 2 and 3, call runner(..., capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300) and use the last non-empty stderr line as `detail`. Write the Makefile recipe as `verify-host:\n\t@$(PYTHON) scripts/check_verify_host.py`. Add test assertions on the runner kwargs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Point the `check_verify_host.py` mechanism-ok marker at a sunset ticket other than d492-04db-b79e-428f, such as a follow-up that retires the preflight once agent sandboxes allow AF_UNIX and package-index/semgrep.dev egress, so this ticket's own close is not blocked by `check_no_open_sunset_marker`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py:3-7: 'An admission now has to name a SUNSET TICKET, and that ticket cannot close while its marker is still in the tree.'

src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py:159-181 `check_no_open_sunset_marker` raises CommandError 'cannot close {ticket_id}: it is named as the sunset ticket of a '# mechanism-ok:' marker still in the tree'
tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py:26-30: 'Seeding a LIVE ticket id here would refuse that ticket's own close forever'
show_ticket confirms d492-04db-b79e-428f is this plan's own ticket id
findings.finding: The plan uses its own ticket as the sunset ticket of the new mechanism-ok marker (`# mechanism-ok: ci_gate scripts/check_verify_host.py — d492-04db-b79e-428f`). The close precheck refuses to close a ticket while a tracked marker names it as its sunset. So this ticket could not close after its own change lands, short of `--force`. The plan treats the marker as a plain admission and does not account for this.
findings.location: Approach — New `scripts/check_verify_host.py` (marked `# mechanism-ok: ci_gate scripts/check_verify_host.py — d492-04db-b79e-428f`)
scenarios: After the change merges, closing d492-04db-b79e-428f is refused because `scripts/check_verify_host.py` still carries a marker naming it.
The only ways out are `--force`, or a second change that repoints or removes the marker, which would undo the admission.
findings.suggested_fix: File a follow-up ticket, for example 'retire make verify host preflight once the agent sandbox grants AF_UNIX + package-index/semgrep.dev egress'. Cite its id as the marker's reason: `# mechanism-ok: ci_gate scripts/check_verify_host.py — <follow-up-id> ...`. Add that ticket to Scope or the plan's deps.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the probe resolves the engine with the same preference order the backend uses (ideally by calling or mirroring its resolver), and test the both-present case.
evidence: "when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes ... otherwise it runs `<engine> --validate ...`"

The claim that the probe 'fails only on what the tests would fail on' holds only if it selects the same engine, in the same preference order, as the backend in `engine_b_backends.py`. Otherwise it can pass or fail on a different binary from the one the tests use.
findings.location: Approach — probe 3 `semgrep_validate_probe`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the plan, either weigh `python -m build --no-isolation` (hatchling and build are already dev dependencies) for tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py, or state why the tests must use an isolated build (e.g. release-workflow parity), and narrow the 'denied capability is the operation under test' claim to match.
evidence: Plan: 'These are not test defects: CI hosts provide both capabilities, and a per-test shim cannot cover them because the denied capability is the operation under test.'
tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py:1-5 docstring: the tests check that the build commit survives the sdist→wheel build; they do not test package-index access.
tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py:28 runs `[sys.executable, '-m', 'build', '--outdir', ...]` without --no-isolation.
pyproject.toml:258,262 already list 'hatchling>=1.27' and 'build>=1.2' as dev dependencies (comment at 259-261: build is also used by the release workflow's build-once job).
findings.finding: For the package index, the plan says a shim cannot help because 'the denied capability is the operation under test'. That is not shown, and it skips a standard alternative: `python -m build --no-isolation`. The tests check that the build hook carries COMMIT from sdist to wheel. Downloading hatchling from pypi.org is not what they test, and hatchling>=1.27 and build>=1.2 are already dev dependencies. The plan neither weighs a no-isolation build nor explains why the tests must run isolated (for example, to match the release workflow's build-once job).
findings.location: Verified cause → 'pypi.org' bullet; closing sentence 'a per-test shim cannot cover them because the denied capability is the operation under test'
scenarios: A developer with a pip cache but no network (on a plane, or behind a corporate proxy) is refused by make verify, though the build-provenance tests could pass offline with --no-isolation.
A brief pypi.org outage turns CI or local verify red for a test unrelated to package fetching.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Verified cause: the isolated build is kept because <reason, e.g. it is what the release job runs and the tests must match it>. Without such a reason, a --no-isolation build would remove the pypi.org dependency and the package_index_probe could go.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the semgrep probe the same timeout the grounding harness applies to `--validate` (60 s default / REBAR_GROUNDING_TIMEOUT), treat TimeoutExpired as a failure, and add a unit test where the semgrep runner raises TimeoutExpired.
evidence: Plan: "validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains"
Plan: "runs `<engine> --validate --config <one-rule temp file> --metrics=off` ... with `timeout=300`"
src/rebar/grounding/harness.py:49 `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60`; run_tool maps TimeoutExpired to abstain_reason="timeout"
src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py:46-49 `_opengrep_validate` calls harness.run_tool with no explicit timeout
Plan: "a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight"
Testing lists only "semgrep runner returning exit 2" for the semgrep probe; there is no TimeoutExpired case for it
findings.finding: The semgrep probe's pass/fail rule does not match what the tests fail on. In the sandbox, `--validate` is cut off by the grounding harness's 60 s timeout (harness.run_tool with _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60, adjustable through REBAR_GROUNDING_TIMEOUT), and the backend then abstains. The probe instead uses timeout=300 and checks the exit code. Three consequences: (a) a host where `--validate` finishes in 60–300 s passes the preflight, yet every grounding test still times out and abstains, which is the false-green/false-red the plan is meant to prevent; (b) in the sandbox the preflight can block for up to 5 minutes before refusing, not the advertised 10 seconds; (c) if semgrep eventually gives up and exits 0 when the lint download fails, the probe passes even though the tests fail.
findings.location: Approach → scripts/check_verify_host.py probe 3 `semgrep_validate_probe`; Testing (semgrep runner cases)
scenarios: Agent sandbox: semgrep keeps retrying the denied semgrep.dev request, so the preflight waits up to 300 s before printing its refusal.
Slow or proxied network outside the sandbox: `--validate` takes about 90 s, the probe passes, and the conflict-marker and conformance tests abstain after 60 s and fail anyway.
The semgrep build falls back after a failed lint download and exits 0: the probe reports OK in the sandbox.
findings.suggested_fix: In semgrep_validate_probe, set the subprocess timeout to the harness's effective timeout (import rebar.grounding.harness._resolve_timeout(None), or read REBAR_GROUNDING_TIMEOUT with a 60 s default) instead of 300. Report TimeoutExpired as 'semgrep rule-lint download from semgrep.dev did not complete within <N> s'. Add a Testing bullet: semgrep runner raising TimeoutExpired is reported as a failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make probes 1 and 2 apply the same 'not applicable → pass' rule the semgrep probe uses: pass the AF_UNIX probe when `socket.AF_UNIX` is absent, and give a missing `build` module its own failure message (or pass) instead of reporting a package-index failure. Add a unit test for each case.
evidence: tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py:25 `pytest.skip("AF_UNIX unavailable on this platform")`
tests/unit/test_reclaim_resign.py:35 `skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="needs a unix-socket ssh-agent")`
tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:424 `skipif(not _has_build(), reason="python -m build not available")`
Plan: "when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine)"
Plan: "A probe that raises unexpectedly is reported as that capability failing"
findings.finding: The probes do not mirror the tests' skip conditions consistently. The semgrep probe passes when no engine is on PATH because those tests skip. The AF_UNIX probe has no equivalent case, even though test_network_guard_local_ipc.py skips with 'AF_UNIX unavailable on this platform' and test_reclaim_resign.py skips on win32 or when ssh-agent is missing. On such a host, `socket.AF_UNIX` raises AttributeError, which the plan reports as a capability failure, so `make verify` is refused for tests that would only skip. Likewise, if the `build` module is not installed, the build probe reports a package-index failure, while test_attestation_signing.py skips with 'python -m build not available'. The capability gets misattributed.
findings.location: Approach → probes 1 and 2 (`unix_socket_probe`, `package_index_probe`)
scenarios: A contributor on a platform without socket.AF_UNIX runs `make verify` and is refused for 'AF_UNIX sockets' even though every AF_UNIX test would skip.
A venv without the `build` package is refused with an error that blames the package index instead of the missing module.
findings.suggested_fix: In unix_socket_probe, return (True, 'not applicable') when `not hasattr(socket, 'AF_UNIX')`. In package_index_probe, check `importlib.util.find_spec('build')` first and either pass (mirroring test_attestation_signing's skip) or fail with a distinct 'python -m build not installed' detail. Add Testing bullets for both.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `unix_socket_probe` pass, with a note in its detail, when `socket.AF_UNIX` is missing, matching the test suite's skip and the no-engine semgrep rule, and add a test for that case.
evidence: tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py:24-25: `if not hasattr(socket, "AF_UNIX"): pytest.skip("AF_UNIX unavailable on this platform")`. The suite skips when the platform has no AF_UNIX.
Plan: 'A probe that raises unexpectedly is reported as that capability failing, with the exception text.' A missing AF_UNIX attribute would hit this path.
Plan, semgrep probe: 'when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine)'. The same skip-parity rule is not applied to AF_UNIX.
The Testing list has no case for 'AF_UNIX unavailable on the platform'.
findings.finding: The AF_UNIX probe does not handle a platform where `socket.AF_UNIX` is missing. On such a host, building the socket raises AttributeError, which the plan's 'a probe that raises unexpectedly is reported as that capability failing' rule turns into a refusal. The tests the probe stands in for skip in that case instead of failing. The plan already applies the matching rule to semgrep ('when neither opengrep nor semgrep is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine)') but not to AF_UNIX. Evidence class: Contradicted for non-POSIX hosts.
findings.location: Approach — probe 1 `unix_socket_probe(socket_factory=socket.socket)`; Testing section
scenarios: A developer runs `make verify-host` or `make verify` on a Windows CPython build, which has no `socket.AF_UNIX`. The preflight refuses with 'AF_UNIX sockets: module socket has no attribute AF_UNIX', even though the AF_UNIX tests there would skip and not diverge from CI.
findings.suggested_fix: In `unix_socket_probe`, return `(True, "AF_UNIX unavailable on this platform; dependent tests skip")` when `not hasattr(socket, "AF_UNIX")`, before calling the factory. Add a test case that simulates the missing attribute through the injected seam.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give unix_socket_probe the same 'not applicable on this platform' pass path the semgrep probe has when `socket.AF_UNIX` is absent (mirroring how the dependent tests behave there), and test it via the seam.
evidence: "`unix_socket_probe(socket_factory=socket.socket)`: bind, listen and connect an AF_UNIX socket"
"when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine)"
Platform fact: CPython on Windows does not define `socket.AF_UNIX`.
findings.finding: unix_socket_probe has no 'tests would skip here' pass path. The semgrep probe has one: it passes when no engine exists because 'those tests skip without an engine'. The AF_UNIX probe has no equivalent, and the plan maps any unexpected exception to 'that capability failing'. On a platform where CPython does not expose `socket.AF_UNIX` (Windows), the probe raises `AttributeError`. That is reported as 'AF_UNIX sockets' denied, and `make verify` refuses on a host where the socket-dependent tests would not be exercising that capability anyway.
findings.location: Approach — probe 1 `unix_socket_probe` and 'A probe that raises unexpectedly is reported as that capability failing'
scenarios: Windows developer workstation: `make verify` exits 1 with 'AF_UNIX sockets: module socket has no attribute AF_UNIX' before lint, instead of running the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: At the top of unix_socket_probe: `if not hasattr(socket, "AF_UNIX"): return True, "AF_UNIX unavailable on this platform; dependent tests skip"`, and add a unit test for that branch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the '10-second' claim with the measured passing and failing durations, and state whether the three probes run sequentially or concurrently (or run them concurrently to bound the worst case at one timeout).
evidence: "a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight"
"with `timeout=300`" (probes 2 and 3)
Context: "validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains"
findings.finding: The plan calls the preflight 'a 10-second preflight', which contradicts the rest of the plan. Each network probe has `timeout=300`, the failing semgrep path is documented to retry for about 60 s, and the build probe runs two isolated-env builds. Whether probes run sequentially or concurrently is also unstated, so the worst case is about 600 s.
findings.location: Approach — probes 2/3 timeouts vs. the 'not retried' rationale
scenarios: In the sandbox (the target case) the refusal takes at least about 60 s, not 10 s.
On a slow or hanging index, the preflight blocks up to 10 minutes before refusing.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the three probes concurrently (e.g. a ThreadPoolExecutor) and state the expected budget: about N s when passing and about 60–300 s when refusing in the sandbox, measured during the manual runs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the three capability label strings in the plan (e.g. 'AF_UNIX sockets', 'outbound HTTPS to the package index (pypi.org)', 'outbound HTTPS to semgrep.dev (rule-lint download)'), use them in Testing and AC 1, and assert them in the main() unit test.
evidence: "Each failed probe prints one line naming the capability and the error detail"
Testing: "naming AF_UNIX sockets and network access"
AC 1: "naming the denied capabilities (AF_UNIX sockets and outbound HTTPS to the package index and semgrep.dev)"

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that every probe uses `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (or try/finally removal), so its temp dir is removed on pass, fail, timeout, and exception.
evidence: Probe 1: "in a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory, then remove it"
Probe 2: "write a minimal throwaway project ... to a temp dir" — no removal stated
Probe 3: "points ... into its temp dir" — no removal stated
findings.finding: Cleanup of the temp directories created by the build and semgrep probes is unspecified. Only the AF_UNIX probe says it removes its directory, and failure or timeout paths are not covered.
findings.location: Approach — probes 2 and 3
scenarios: Every `make verify` leaks a build tree and semgrep log dir into TMPDIR, including after timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each probe's work in `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:` so cleanup runs on every exit path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that every probe creates its scratch dir with `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (or try/finally `shutil.rmtree`) so it is removed on pass, fail, timeout, and exception, and add a test that the dir is gone after the failure path.
evidence: "bind, listen and connect an AF_UNIX socket in a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory, then remove it" (cleanup stated for probe 1 only)
"write a minimal throwaway project ... to a temp dir" / "points `SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE` and `SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` into its temp dir" — no removal stated
findings.finding: Only unix_socket_probe states that its temp directory is removed. package_index_probe writes a project plus an sdist and wheel `--outdir`, and semgrep_validate_probe writes a rule file plus redirected settings and log files. Neither states that its temp dir is removed, including on timeout or exception paths. These dirs accumulate in TMPDIR on every `make verify`.
findings.location: Approach — probes 2 and 3
scenarios: An agent or developer running `make verify` repeatedly leaves one build tree and one semgrep dir per run under TMPDIR.
A probe hitting `TimeoutExpired` leaves its partial build output behind.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each probe's scratch area in `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:` and assert in tests that the injected runner's tmp path no longer exists after the probe returns.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the '10-second' claim with the real expected and worst-case durations, and state whether the probes run sequentially or concurrently; consider running them concurrently and/or a shorter per-probe timeout.
evidence: "validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains"
"with `timeout=300`" (probe 2) and "with `timeout=300`" (probe 3)
"a re-run of a 10-second preflight"
findings.finding: The plan justifies 'no retry' by calling the preflight 'a 10-second preflight'. Its own facts contradict that. In the sandbox, semgrep `--validate` retries for about 60 s before failing. Each of the two network probes has `timeout=300`, so a slow or hanging index or semgrep.dev can hold the preflight for up to ~10 minutes if the probes run sequentially. Run order and parallelism are not stated, and the worst-case latency is not bounded or surfaced to the user while it waits.
findings.location: Approach — 'The probes are not retried: a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight'
scenarios: Inside the agent sandbox, the very case the plan targets, the semgrep probe alone takes ~60 s before refusing.
On a host with a stalled proxy, both network probes hang to their 300 s timeouts back-to-back with no output.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure-disposition statement per probe: AF_UNIX/permission denial = permanent (run elsewhere); network timeout/connection error = transient (re-run). Make the printed line (or exit code) carry that disposition rather than one blanket exit 1 with a 'run elsewhere' message.
evidence: "Exit 1 on any failure, 0 and no output otherwise."
"a transient network failure costs a re-run"
"run it where they are available (for an agent sandbox, outside it)"
findings.finding: The preflight adds a new refusal path, but every failure collapses to exit 1 with no stated disposition. A permanent host limitation (AF_UNIX `PermissionError`, `deny network-outbound`) and a transient one (an index timeout or network blip, which the plan itself says 'costs a re-run') surface identically. The plan never states, per probe, whether its failure is permanent (move hosts) or transient (retry). The closing line always says to run elsewhere, even for a transient timeout.
findings.location: Approach — 'Exit 1 on any failure' / closing line
scenarios: An agent sees exit 1 from a pypi `TimeoutExpired` and abandons local verify for an unsandboxed host when a simple re-run would pass.
The operator's verify-slot wrapper cannot tell 'retry later' from 'this host can never verify'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reuse or extract one shared Makefile target parser (header prerequisites plus tab-indented recipe) for the new ordering test instead of adding a third private `_recipe` copy next to test_install_extras_parity.py and test_typecheck_scope.py.
evidence: tests/unit/test_install_extras_parity.py:41 `def _recipe(makefile: str, target: str) -> str:` (regex-based, returns the recipe body)
tests/unit/test_typecheck_scope.py:16 `def _recipe(target: str, text: str) -> str:` (line-based, returns the header plus the tab-indented body)
The new test needs both the prerequisites from the header and the recipe body, and must not confuse `verify:` with `verify-host:`. That is a third variant of the same parsing.
findings.finding: The planned Makefile-ordering test would be the third separate copy of a Makefile recipe parser in the test suite. Two private `_recipe` helpers already do this job with slightly different behaviour, so this is the point to extract one shared helper (Rule of Three) instead of writing another copy.
findings.location: Testing — 'A test parses the Makefile and asserts `verify`'s only prerequisite is `verify-host` and its recipe runs `lint typecheck import-convention test`'
scenarios: The three copies drift. For example, one regex `^verify:` copy is later adapted carelessly and matches the wrong target, or handles `@$(MAKE)` sub-make lines differently from the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Move a header-plus-recipe parser (based on tests/unit/test_typecheck_scope.py:_recipe, which already returns the `<target>:` header line) into a shared test helper module and have the new test split the header on ':' to read the prerequisites. Optionally point the two existing callers at it as well.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Verified cause, name the two failing AF_UNIX tests in `test_network_guard_local_ipc.py` (the af_unix_connect and forkserver tests) instead of saying 'both tests' of a module that has 6.
evidence: tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py defines test_network_guard_allows_af_unix_connect (l.20), test_network_guard_still_blocks_real_tcp (l.45), test_network_guard_allows_the_stdlib_loopback_socketpair (l.59), test_network_guard_allows_an_event_loop_on_the_windows_socketpair (l.77), test_network_guard_still_blocks_a_loopback_connect_from_test_code (l.95), test_network_guard_allows_forkserver_multiprocessing (l.119)
findings.finding: The Context says AF_UNIX denial breaks 'both tests in `tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py`'. The file actually has 6 tests. Only some of them use AF_UNIX: `test_network_guard_allows_af_unix_connect` and `test_network_guard_allows_forkserver_multiprocessing`. The count is wrong as worded, though the 2-test failure figure may still be accurate.
findings.location: Verified cause — AF_UNIX sockets bullet
scenarios: A reviewer or a later doc update copies 'both tests in the module' and wrongly concludes the whole module is AF_UNIX-dependent.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'both tests in `tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py`' to '2 of its 6 tests (`test_network_guard_allows_af_unix_connect`, `test_network_guard_allows_forkserver_multiprocessing`) in `tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py`'. First confirm against the A/B log that these are the two that failed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the plan, consider offline detector validation (parse/schema check without the p/semgrep-rule-lints download, as in the upstream semgrep/opengrep issues) as an alternative to refusing hosts without semgrep.dev access, and either adopt it (perhaps in a follow-up ticket) or state why the rule-lint download must stay on the validate path.
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py:39-49: _opengrep_validate runs `--validate --config <f> --metrics=off` on the product path, not only in tests.
Plan: 'validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains' and 'their negative tests pass falsely after 122 s each'.
findings.finding: For semgrep.dev, the plan calls the network fetch a host capability that CI supplies. It does not consider the documented prior art showing that the fetch comes from a hard-coded `p/semgrep-rule-lints` in `--validate`, nor the common workaround: offline validation that parses and schema-checks the rule (for example, scanning an empty target and reading the parse or schema error) and drops the rule lints. Because _opengrep_validate is production code, the same ~60 s retry and abstention also hits rebar users in restricted networks. Either the engine's dependency on the network or the host can be treated as the defect, and the plan does not say why it chose the host.
findings.location: Verified cause → 'semgrep.dev' bullet; Approach item 3 (semgrep_validate_probe)
scenarios: A rebar user running grounding or code review in a network-restricted CI hits the same 60 s retry and silent abstention (false negatives). The preflight only protects make verify.
A semgrep.dev outage or change to the rule-lint pack makes CI's verdict depend on an outside service.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the '10-second preflight' claim with a measured duration for both a healthy host and the sandbox. If the measured time matters, run the three probes concurrently or lower the network probe timeouts, and state the worst-case wall time.
evidence: Plan, Verified cause: 'validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains'.
Plan: probe 2 and probe 3 each use `timeout=300`. Nothing says the probes run concurrently.
Plan: 'a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight, not of a 25-minute suite'.
test_build_provenance.py:28 shows the probe repeats a full isolated sdist build plus a wheel build.
findings.finding: The plan calls the preflight 'a 10-second preflight', but its own evidence and design contradict that. In the sandbox, the plan says semgrep `--validate` 'retries for about 60 s' before failing. The probes run in sequence, each with `timeout=300`, so the worst case is about 10 minutes. On a healthy host, `python -m build` (an isolated env install of hatchling for the sdist, then a second one for the wheel built from it) plus a semgrep.dev ruleset download is unlikely to finish in 10 s. Evidence class: Unverified, and Contradicted by the plan's own 60 s retry measurement.
findings.location: Approach — 'The probes are not retried: a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight'; probes 2 and 3 `timeout=300`
scenarios: Inside the agent sandbox, the preflight takes at least 60 s on semgrep alone, plus pip's retries against pypi.org, before it prints the refusal.
On a slow or flaky network, a healthy host waits up to 2 × 300 s before the gates start.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the three probes concurrently, for example with `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`, since each is I/O-bound and independent. Record the measured preflight time for a healthy host and for the sandbox on the ticket next to the acceptance evidence, and state the result in the plan instead of '10-second'.
